newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares end 0.54pct up, seen stabilising.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares end 0.54pct up, seen stabilising.

text.p: The Athens bourse settled 0.54 percent higher on Tuesday after suffering heavy losses for three consecutive sessions and market watchers predicted the market would stabilise this week.
"The market was very volatile today and directionless," said Vassilis Antoniadis, an analyst at Diethniki Mutual Funds. "I expect it to consolidate this week."
Some institutional investors and banks intervened intra-day to support their shares helping drive the benchmark index higher, analysts said.
The bank sectoral index posted losses of 2.10 percent but banks belonging to the group of the state National Bank of Greece, the state Macedonia-Thrace bank and the Bank of Central Greece rose.
OTE also put on a strong performance rising 190 drachmas to close at 5,590 drachmas.
The market has overreacted recently because some investors have based their investment decisions on psychology rather than fundamentals, Antoniadis added.
"I hope the index does not drop again this week. If it falls below 1,100 points then we will be in trouble," he said.

The Athens general share index ended 0.54 percent or 6.48 points higher at 1213.02 points from Monday's 1206.54, after opening at 1200.15. The session's high was at 1234.96 points and its low at 1159.09.

"It was a relief to see the benchmark index close higher today," said Yannis Kalogerakis, head of sales and trading at ABN-AMRO Axias Securities. "I expect the general index to stabilise in the 1,200-1,250 range for a few days before heading higher."
Turnover was 23.8 billion drachmas on volume of 5.7 million shares. Advancers led decliners 148 to 73 with 14 issues unchanged on 235 traded.
Industrial stocks settled 3.05 higher and leasing shares gained 7.11 percent and construction shares lost 2.15 percent.
Investment shares lost 0.22 percent. Insurance stocks closed 1.72 percent higher and small caps ended 0.81 percent.
